page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 34 GB of local temporary SSD storage without bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight competent single-threaded capability contrasted against limited aggregate throughput dictated by the 2-vCPU ceiling. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server achieved 2703.88 points, landing in the top 25%. However, overall multi-core performance sits in the lower percentiles, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 1959.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3148.93. Memory throughput reflects 32.67 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.32 GB/sec for writes. Throughput metrics reflect its entry-tier scale, managing 2.03 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.48 GB/sec in static web serving.

From an efficiency standpoint, the E2as_v4 offers an economical entry tier for applications demanding high memory capacity relative to compute footprint. It trades raw compute scalability for memory density, making it less suited for compute-intensive tasks or parallel compilation workloads. Workload fit includes small relational databases, memory caching layers, low-traffic web backends, background job runners, and lightweight development environments requiring up to 16 GB of working memory.
